channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: CoreWeave Plans to Raise at Least $4 Billion in High-Grade Loan
item.description: CoreWeave Inc. plans to raise at least $4 billion through an investment-grade loan offering after the AI computing supplier boosted its annual sales forecast, easing investor concerns about its debt-laden business.
item.dc:creator: Jeannine Amodeo

item.title: Huang Said to Have Had Affair With Nvidia Executive: NYT
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care, according to the New York Times. Michael Shepard has more on "Balance of Power: Evening Edition." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Preparing to Oust Jensen Huang After Affairs, WSJ Says
item.description: Nvidia Corp.’s board is preparing to oust Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang after multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman who is reportedly suspected of being a Chinese spy, the Wall Street Journal said Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Lynn Doan

item.title: Stocks Slide as AI Trade Roars Back | Closing Bell
item.description: Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Romaine Bostick, Vonnie Quinn, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: OpenAI, Anthropic Valuations Fuel VC Fears of Startup Correction
item.description: In late September, OpenAI entered discussions for its latest funding round with confidence. After having early discussions with prospective backers who had expressed interest, the company presented its terms: at least $30 billion in new capital at a $1.4 trillion valuation.Few startups have been as successful at fundraising as OpenAI, which was last valued at $852 billion. This time, however, some investors felt the terms were too lofty, according to people familiar with the matter, who spoke on
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Torrence and Natasha Mascarenhas

item.title: Microsoft Vows to Pay Its Own Way to Power Data Centers
item.description: Microsoft Corp. aims to find ways to power its data centers without relying on government subsidies or driving up costs for other electricity consumers.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Crowley

item.title: Huang's Ties to Trump Under Scrutiny After Spy Claim
item.description: Bloomberg's Mike Shepard said that actions taken by the Trump administration and by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang are coming under sharper scrutiny by Congress amid investigations into the affair Huang had with a women alleged to be a Chinese spy. Trump had denied that he knew anything about the national security risks posed by Huang's affair, but recent New York Times reporting reveals that Trump had been briefed about the risk before his trip to China earlier this year. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rubenstein on the Anthropic IPO, Nvidia CEO Scandal
item.description: Carlyle Group co-Chairman and Bloomberg Host David Rubenstein talks about the anticipated initial public offering of Anthropic and the scandal involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. He expects the Anthropic valuation to reach $1.3 trillion and he thinks Huang will stay on as leader of Nvidia. Rubenstein also talks about the upcoming release of Grand Theft Auto VI. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Expect ‘Dislocations’ in AI Investment Cycle: Waxman
item.description: Alan Waxman, CEO and co-founder of Sixth Street, joins Dani Burger on “Bloomberg Deals.” They discuss dislocations he is seeing in the AI market. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Oura to Buy AI Doctor Startup
item.description: Oura agreed to acquire AI and on-demand doctor service Counsel Health for $625 million, expanding its business following a scrapped attempt to go public. Scarlet Fu and Dani Burger discuss the acquisition on this week’s edition of “Bloomberg Deals.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Adobe Is Helping Disney with Custom AI Tools
item.description: Adobe and Disney have entered a multi-year partnership to help develop custom AI models and tools that the entertainment giant can use across its theme parks, studio and sports media businesses. Deepa Subramaniam, Vice President of Product Marketing for Creative Professionals at Adobe, explains how it all works with Riley Griffin on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Take-Two’s Zelnick on Success of the GTA Franchise
item.description: Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick talks about the highly anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto VI, out next week. He says the Grand Theft Auto franchise “is probably the most valuable intellectual property in the entertainment business” because of its enormous global reach. Zelnick sits down with David Rubenstein on this week’s episode of The David Rubenstein Show: Peer to Peer Conversations. This interview was recorded October 19 in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia China Scandal Demands Answers, Says Congressman
item.description: Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi says Congress needs answers from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over his reported relationship with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence, and says lawmakers could consider a subpoena if Huang doesn’t voluntarily appear. The Illinois Democrat also calls for a review of Nvidia’s China export licenses and tougher controls designed to prevent advanced US chips from reaching restricted Chinese entities. He joins Riley Griffin on “Bloomberg Tech.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Military, Congress Focus on Toll of Cyber Jobs Following Suicides
item.description: At least 11 workers at NSA and Cyber Command have taken their own lives in last year or so.
item.dc:creator: Jake Bleiberg

item.title: Google Adds Gemini Voice AI Assistant to Apple CarPlay
item.description: Alphabet Inc.’s Google is adding its Gemini artificial intelligence app to Apple Inc.’s CarPlay system, expanding options for drivers who may already be using the assistant on their Apple devices.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Lung

item.title: Suicides Raise Alarm Inside US Cybersecurity Agencies
item.description: At least 11 National Security Agency and US Cyber Command workers died by suicide over roughly the past year, according to US officials and public records. Bloomberg’s Jake Bleiberg discusses the intense workload facing personnel at the NSA and Cyber Command amid global conflicts, why the death are raising concerns among senior officials in Congress and the White House, and the efforts to increase mental health support for a workforce critical to US national security. He joins Riley Griffin on “Bloomberg Tech.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: United Blocks AI Agents From Booking Flights Ahead of Holidays
item.description: United Airlines Holdings Inc. is moving to block third-party artificial intelligence agents from booking flights and accessing customer accounts ahead of the holiday travel season, as the growing use of AI in the airline industry raises concerns about privacy.
item.dc:creator: Sri Taylor

item.title: Anthropic IPO Demand Surges as CoreWeave Calms AI Fears
item.description: Bloomberg’s Riley Griffin takes a look at Anthropic's potentially record-breaking IPO, with sources saying it's already multiple times oversubscribed. Plus, CoreWeave reassures Wall Street with third-quarter sales topping analyst estimates and easing fears about the debt tied to its rapid AI buildout; and Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi discusses how the Nvidia scandal is felt across Washington and beyond. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Odd Lots: The AI Trade Shrugs Off a Blue Wave and a Tech Scandal
item.description:
It’s been a big month so far for American politics and the tech industry. Democrats deliver a sweeping win across the country, calling continued AI development into question. Nvidia launches an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy. There are plenty of things to make investors jittery, yet we’re seeing a tech rally as markets await the upcoming Anthropic IPO.
Bloomberg’s Michael Ball joins Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway on the Odd Lots podcast to unpack why the tech trade is showing resilience despite macro jitters. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: CoreWeave Soars After AI Computing Firm Eases Debt Fears
item.description: CoreWeave Inc. shares soared the most in 17 months after the AI computing supplier eased fears about its debt-laden business and signaled that sales growth remains strong despite the many headwinds facing the data center boom.
item.dc:creator: Dina Bass and Brody Ford
